items.description: Defense attorneys for the man accused of assassinating conservative activist Charlie Kirk are suggesting a 2029 trial date because they say it could take them that long to prepare their case.

items.title: Connacht secure bonus-point win over Zebre
items.description: Connacht return to winning ways in the United Rugby Championship with an eight-try 48-27 victory over Zebre at Dexcom Stadium.

items.title: 'It doesn't make sense' - Glasner confused after Diop avoids red card
items.description: Nottingham Forest manager Oliver Glasner admits he was left confused by the decision to not send off Issa Diop after a VAR check during his side's 1-1 draw at Ipswich Town, but praised his side's performance and urged them to 'stay patient' as Forest's winless run stretched to four matches.

items.title: 'That's what I do' - Wade scores again to equal Prem try-scoring record
items.description: Christian Wade has equalled the Prem Rugby try-scoring record, level on 101 with Chris Ashton, and the Newcastle winger has shown no signs of slowing down.

items.title: 'We had to scrap' - O'Neil praises Ipswich resilience after Forest draw
items.description: Ipswich manager Gary O'Neil praises his side's ability to "dig in and fight" as his side come from behind to earn a 1-1 draw against Nottingham Forest at Portman Road in the Premier League.

items.title: Who actually controls Ukraine's access to Starlink?
items.description: President Zelensky says limits to the technology continue to affect Ukrainian forces, while US officials and Elon Musk offer conflicting accounts of who controls it.

items.title: Why 'You Can See Everything' is captivating audiences
items.description: "You Can See Everything," the documentary co-directed by Lance Oppenheim and Nathan Fielder, is a breakthrough success. It follows Elizabeth Holmes, the convicted founder of Theranos, just weeks before she goes to prison. The intimate access and the questions it raises are the talk of this fall movie season. Jeffrey Brown sat down with Alissa Wilkinson for our arts and culture series, CANVAS.

items.title: Medicare Advantage cuts leave millions scrambling to find coverage
items.description: Health care costs are climbing, putting new pressure on millions of Americans and raising questions about the coverage they can afford. The challenges extend to Medicare Advantage. In some parts of the country, insurers are pulling out of markets or eliminating plans that many rely on. We hear from seniors struggling to navigate those changes, and Geoff Bennett discusses more with Dan Weissmann.

items.title: Brazil's high-stakes presidential runoff could reshape country's future
items.description: This weekend, voters in Brazil head to the polls in a high-stakes presidential runoff that could reshape that country's political future. Will Brazil join a rightward shift across parts of the Americas, or stick with its left-wing leadership? Voting is compulsory for most adults, and the race has deepened political divisions across the country. Stephanie Sy reports.

items.title: At a Texas high school football game, fans offer a glimpse into evolving politics
items.description: We talk with voters at a Texas high school football game at the tailgate, in line at the concession booth and in the stands to hear about the issues that matter to Texans this cycle.

items.title: Capehart and Ponnuru on Trump's threat to block Alaska election results
items.description: Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW and National Review editor Ramesh Ponnuru join Geoff Bennett to discuss the week in politics, including the Trump administration's legal fight over a closely watched Senate race in Alaska, reports that Elon Musk restricted Ukraine's access to Starlink and Vivek Ramaswamy's personal ad attacking his opponent in the Ohio governor's race.

items.title: Surging diesel prices loom over Republicans in Iowa's midterm races
items.description: It's been more than a decade since Iowa has had a Democratic governor or senator. But this year, with the incumbents retiring, both races are competitive. As Peter Tubbs at Iowa PBS reports, record-high diesel prices have hit the state's agriculture industry particularly hard and could influence the midterm elections.

items.title: Father who killed Oregon school shooter describes anguish over children he couldn't save
items.description: Kaylub Giamanco, has been hailed as a hero for killing a teenager who fatally shot three children and a teacher.

items.title: Seeking to help Collins in Maine, Trump exempts some Canadian imports from his 50% tariffs
items.description: Collins, locked in a tight race with Democratic challenger Troy Jackson, issued a statement saying she'd spoken with Trump's top trade negotiator, Jamieson Greer, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick "about the toll tariffs are taking on Maine families, businesses, farmers, and growers.''

items.title: 'There's babies in there': Oregon father describes stopping school shooter
items.description: Kaylub Giamanco is the father who stopped a school shooter in Bend, Oregon, a week ago. The teen gunman entered the school and killed three students and a teacher before Giamanco stopped him. In a new interview with Oregon Public Broadcasting, Giamanco describes the moments leading up to his heroic actions, how he felt after he took down the shooter and that day's larger tragedy.

items.title: Wilson and Williams through to NI Open semi-finals
items.description: Former Northern Ireland Open champions Mark Williams and Kyren Wilson win through to the semi-finals of this year's tournament in Belfast.

items.title: News Wrap: White House says Melania Trump brokered localized ceasefire deal in Oleshky
items.description: In our news wrap Friday, the White House says Melania Trump brokered a localized ceasefire deal in the Ukrainian city of Oleshky, Romania's president blamed Russia for a drone strike that sank a cargo ship in the Black Sea and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu ordered the army there to prepare for a full closure of the occupied West Bank.

items.title: Celebrity Traitors left on a knife edge after a trip to the field of screams
items.description: A newly earned special power left one contestant with a big decision to make in Friday's episode.

items.title: Trump says he ordered suit to block Alaska Senate results if GOP loses
items.description: President Trump is making a final push to help Republicans maintain control of Congress as some of the most closely watched races remain competitive. But the battle for the Senate is also playing out in court. In Alaska, the Trump administration sued to potentially block certification of the election if the Republican incumbent loses. White House correspondent Liz Landers reports.

items.title: Two doctors offer new ideas to prevent gun violence in America
items.description: America has an epidemic of gun violence that claims over 120 people every day. The country has debated what to do about this for years, but little has changed. Horizons moderator William Brangham explores gun safety and public health with Dr. Sandy McKay and Dr. Joseph Sakran, two experts with prevention ideas they argue every American can get behind.

items.title: The artist dropping her debut album after a billion streams
items.description: Irish DJ Jazzy came up on the Dublin club scene and has worked with industry heavyweights like Calvin Harris.

items.title: The latest in space science: We look back at the Big Bang
items.description: In this edition of Spacing Out, the team from Short Wave shares the latest developments in space science, including the theory on why the universe is made of matter

items.title: Strictly's new presenters - after frosty reviews have they warmed up?
items.description: Josh Widdicombe, Emma Willis and Johannes Radebe have split opinion but are getting into the groove, critics say.

items.title: Treasury proposes rule to curb high-tech investments in China and other adversaries
items.description: The U.S. Treasury Department proposed a rule Thursday to crack down on American high-tech investments such as supercomputing and artificial intelligence in China, Russia, North Korea and other "countries of concern."

items.title: Why some U.S. allies view Trump's America as an 'Unreliable Boyfriend'
items.description: Behind closed diplomatic doors, some of the U.S.'s closest allies view Donald Trump's America as an "unreliable boyfriend", a "security threat," and open to corruption. A Canadian official warns that the world's disappointment with the U.S. will have long-lasting consequences. Compass Points moderator Nick Schifrin discusses more with Chrystia Freeland, the former deputy prime minister of Canada.

items.title: Signs of fraying loyalty emerge in Netanyahu stronghold before Israeli election
items.description: Kiryat Shmona, Israel's northernmost city, has long been a bastion of support for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party. But that loyalty is no longer ironclad.

items.title: Leclerc fastest from Antonelli in US GP practice
items.description: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc leads Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli in Friday practice at the United States Grand Prix.

items.title: Before you crank up the thermostat, try these tips to keep your house warmer for longer
items.description: Make draught excluders from socks, leave your oven door open after cooking and opt for lots of thin layers of clothing to stay warm.

items.title: Rollins says USDA is 'full-bore ahead' on Forest Service reorganization
items.description: The Trump administration wants to move Forest Service headquarters from Washington to Salt Lake City, shutter 23 research stations, and close many regional offices and replace them with state offices.

items.title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab
items.description: The chancellor will unveil AI spending aimed at shoring up the UK's defences in Wednesday's Budget.

items.title: How does the UK state pension compare with other countries?
items.description: Do British pensioners have it better or worse than those in other countries?

items.title: White House lifts tariffs on some Canadian goods as midterm elections loom
items.description: From 30 October, tariffs will be eased on some products, including certain machinery, and placed on others, such as carpets.

items.title: Severe flooding hits Four Corners region, more expected through the weekend
items.description: Intense rainfall slammed the Four Corners region late this week. As rivers flooded, towns declared evacuations and emergencies and made rescues.

items.title: England suffer back-to-back losses to Canada
items.description: Watch highlights as England were beaten by Canada for the second time in as many weeks, losing 31-22 in their WXV Global Series match in Ottawa, Canada.

items.title: Second storm to hit UK with more wind and rain as thousands remain without power
items.description: An amber weather warning has been issued for much of Scotland, parts of Northern Ireland and northern England, as Storm Boelo approaches.

items.title: Arrest made after fire at Hitler's Eagle's Nest retreat
items.description: Around 200 emergency personnel are deployed to fight the blaze at the Nazi dictator's Alpine residence in Germany.
